prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: offshore-wind acceptance/O&M/refurbishment/decommissioning; excludes beyond-connection grid/unrelated ports. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal; Foxglove=Emergency Generator. Elements: Pitch System; Converter Cabinet; Nacelle Condition Monitor; Rotor Brake Unit; Turbine Sensor Bus; Main Transformer; Export Cable Monitor; Daughter Craft; Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; North Access Scanner; South Access Scanner; Personnel Tracking Console; Spares Hub. Actors: SCADA Engineer; Marine Coordinator; Vessel Master; Duty Planner; Weather Analyst; Blade Specialist; Field Supervisor; Storekeeper; Port Agent; HSE Officer; technical reviewers. Items: Turbine Controller reports Pitch Deviation Notice; Vessel AIS Receiver timestamps broadcasts/produces Position Quality Flag; Duty Planner produces Transfer Manifest Addendum; Warehouse System produces Backorder Exception Slip; validated Metocean Buoy observations feed Weather Service/Squall Window Bulletin; buoy produces Wave Burst Record at configured intervals. Requirements: authorized/logged/bounded commands; local-protection precedence; Weather Hold resumes confirmed-safe; unsafe drone flights suspended; physical inspections retained; permits retain auditable lifecycle, require complete requests/reviews/controls and bounded authorization. Normal mode: station service transformers supply auxiliary loads; essential/nonessential separation. Supply-loss automatically starts generator; emergency-bus transfer requires acceptable voltage/frequency; parallel sources prohibited without approved synchronization. Generator supports emergency loads, not turbine exports; prioritize safety/protection/shutdown; automatically shed excess nonessential loads. Start/stabilization failure alarms; retain available uninterruptible control power. Operators follow approved safe recovery. Electrical Technician verifies protection/interlocks; scheduled exercising verifies start/load/duration; readiness checks fuel/cooling/lubrication/battery/exhaust. Maintenance Planning Engine schedules condition/history-based work. Offshore Substation maintains bus limits; Grid Interface Relay indicates supply/protection; Turbine Controller enters configured safe mode without required auxiliaries; SCADA Gateway sends alarms/status to Shore Control Room; Control Engineer coordinates persistent-alarm support with

New part:
S195: Thistle Crown schedules periodic reviews of standby electrical maintenance requirements and outstanding corrective work.
S196: After normal supply is restored, transfer back is permitted only after stable conditions are confirmed and the emergency source can be unloaded safely.
S197: The Grid Interface Relay defines the operational boundary between the offshore farm and the external transmission system.
S198: Grid Interface Relay is known operationally as Wildmere.
S199: The farm exports electrical power through the Offshore Substation, Main Transformer, and export cable to the designated grid connection point.
S200: The Export Cable Monitor provides measurements that support assessment of the export path.
S201: The Grid Interface Relay exchanges authorized operating signals with the transmission system at the agreed interface.
S202: The Grid Dispatcher sets external dispatch requirements within the applicable connection agreement.
S203: The Fleet Dispatch Console allocates requested farm output among available generating units.
S204: Dispatch commands remain subject to equipment capability, protection settings, and approved operating limits.
S205: The farm reports measured active power at the grid boundary for operational monitoring and settlement processes.
S206: Reactive power capability is managed in accordance with the connection agreement and current equipment conditions.
S207: Frequency response functions are enabled only when the relevant operating mode is authorized and available.
S208: Protection coordination prevents a fault on the external system from causing unnecessary disconnection of healthy farm equipment.
S209: Loss of communications does not remove local electrical protection or equipment interlocks.
S210: A Grid Constraint may require reduced export, revised dispatch, or temporary disconnection.
S211: SCADA Gateway provides relay status and interface measurements to the farm monitoring environment.
S212: SCADA Gateway produces the Session Revocation Receipt when an authenticated control session is terminated.
S213: Maintenance Planning Engine uses the Squall Window Bulletin when reviewing the timing of planned work.
S214: Amber Quay coordinates operational notices and control-room decisions affecting the farm interface.
S215: Kestrel Bay reports its approach and departure status in accordance with the approved marine coordination procedure.
S216: The Substation Operator confirms that switching actions affecting the export path are within the authorized work scope.
S217: The Control Engineer verifies that dispatch changes are reflected in the applicable control settings before implementation.
S218: Interface alarms are prioritized according to their effect on safety, equipment protection, and continuity of export.
S219: Planned tests are coordinated to avoid conflicting with dispatch obligations or active maintenance work.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
